text:
Emily: heads-up — since last night's runtime rollout we're seeing a sharp drop in the lead-in (prefix) cache cold-start hit rate for a subset of production traffic. baseline ~78% -> 14% on first 10 tokens for many long-chat prompts. first noticed ~0300 UTC.

Raj: ack. which rollout exactly? kernel heuristic refactor + quant profile flip?

deploy-bot: deployed runtime/serve commit abc123def (attn_v2_refactor + quant-profile-v3) to cluster-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T23:45:12Z (deploy id dpl-20260317-17).

Emily: yes that deploy. quick numbers from our cost dashboard: 
- traffic slice "conversational-long": prefix_hit_rate before=0.78 after=0.14 (5-10k samples)
- avg latency +12ms on first token, p50 unaffected after warmup window

Zoe: do we have evidence it's a keying/normalization change vs genuine cache eviction? any log that prints computed prefix key?

Emily: added a quick debug trace to one instance and repro'd with recorded prompts. sample log snippet:
```
PFX_KEY: digest=0x9f3a1b, normalizer=v1, pad_order=lhs, prefix_len=32, hit=false
PFX_KEY: digest=0x9f3a1b, normalizer=v2, pad_order=rhs, prefix_len=32, hit=false
```
looks like different normalizer/pad ordering in the runtime variant.

Raj: hmm pad_order flip would totally change keyspace. did the kernel refactor change how we serialize attention MX shapes?

Nate: I have a hunch: attn_v2_refactor changed the KV flatten order to improve memory lanes (N, H, L) -> (H, N, L) and quant-profile-v3 introduced a tiny token-level rounding change. together they change the prefix key canonicalization.

Kyle: can we confirm by running the same input on old binary vs new binary and diff the raw keys? I can run a batch of 1k traces. command I used last time:
```
# generate keys for trace set
python infra/tools/prefix_key_dump.py --input traces/20260317-conv.jsonl --binary /opt/redwood/bin/runtime-old --out keys-old.ndjson
python infra/tools/prefix_key_dump.py --input traces/20260317-conv.jsonl --binary /opt/redwood/bin/runtime-new --out keys-new.ndjson
ndiff keys-old.ndjson keys-new.ndjson | head
```

perf-bot: perf job queued: perf/diff-prefix-keys/dpl-20260317-17 (you will get results in ~12m).

Zoe: also check tokenizer normalization or model token_map changes — sometimes quantized emb lookups use alt detokenization paths that change prefix chunking.

Emily: tokenization unchanged (confirmed against model repo tag v1.4.2). I think this is runtime-level canonicalization. debug dump shows the serialized prefix bytes differ before hashing (visible in logs).

Raj: critical question — is it only cold-start with cross-batch ordering? or does in-memory KV eviction behave differently? i.e. are keys produced consistent per instance but mapping different across instances?

Emily: preliminary answer: keys are inconsistent between binaries (same input produces different serialized bytes -> different digest). within the new binary, keys are consistent across instances (no non-determinism); it just canonicalizes differently.

Nate: that suggests a compatibility shim is needed for rolling upgrades. two options: 1) canonicalize keys to a stable on-disk representation (slow but correct), 2) add a compatibility map between old->new digests for a grace period.

Kyle: also measuring the warmup window impact — because dedupe/warmup heuristics were tweaked, we now batch earlier and that reduces opportunity for local prefix cache hits before requests hit remote store. batching change could lower observed pref hits as well.

Emily: true — I ran a controlled run disabling batching heuristics (old behaviour) and hit rate went to 62% on same new binary. so both factors matter: serialization change (~drop to 20%) + batching tweak (~drop further to 14%).

Zoe: do we have an easy mitigation we can deploy quickly? rollback quant-profile-v3? rollback kernel heuristics? or add key canonicalization shim?

Raj: fastest path to restore unit economics: roll kernel heuristic refactor back for canary clusters (rollback dpl-20260317-17). quant profile rollback is lower-risk but we also want kernel fixes upstream.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for cluster-us-west-2 canaries (dpl-rollback dpl-20260317-17). ETA ~8m.

perf-bot: perf/diff-prefix-keys completed: 1k traces compared -> 412 keys mismatched solely due to padding order, 321 mismatched due to byte-serialization reorder, remainder due to quant rounding differences.

Kyle: attaching the key-diff summary (uploaded to s3): s3://redwood-perf/prefix-key-diffs/3501234567-summary.json

Emily: next steps I propose:
- immediate: keep rollback for canaries + monitor prefix hit rate (Raj/Kyle)
- short-term (48h): add canonicalizer layer in runtime that normalizes pad_order & flatten axis ordering before hashing (Nate owns)
- mid-term (2w): add migration map/compatibility mode that accepts old digests for a TTL (Zoe owns)
- tests: add unit test that runs both old/new binary key generation and asserts stable digest for a set of golden prompts (Emily owns)

Nate: I'll open a PR with a small pure-python canonicalizer for review today and wire it behind a flag so we can A/B it.

Raj: sounds good. Emily/Kyle please post the monitoring dashboard links and I'll keep on-call looped. also let's add an alert for prefix_hit_rate_delta > 0.15.

Emily: dashboard: https://console.redwood.io/dashboards/prefix-cache?slice=conversational-long (watching). created alert: /alerts/prefix-hit-drop (severity=high).

Zoe: one more ask — capture 10 raw serialized prefix bytes for mismatched keys and upload to the ticket so model team can sanity-check (possible tokenizer edge-case).

Emily: noted, will upload traces to the ticket RDW-9876. thanks all. :thumbsup:
